Automatic API Security Design Review · Phases 1–4

trainticket: threat graph with propagated risk

Every finding below comes from the four discovery sources, merged into one API inventory and checked by 27 deterministic rules. Each one names the standard it is based on and how to fix it.

Insight

  • The single most valuable fix is Set auth: required on gateway route /api/v1/adminbasicservice.: it removes 21.8% of attack-path risk on its own.
  • 58 of 166 remediation actions remove 70% of the attack-path risk; 115 remove 90%.
  • 9 of 263 endpoints are in no API spec; 7 of them carry critical or high findings. A spec-only review would have missed them.
  • 184 of 236 findings are backed by two or more independent sources (spec, traffic, manifests, traces).
  • 43 critical attack paths start from the internet. The shortest has 4 hops.
  • Highest propagated risk: ts-gateway-service (21.25/25), the service whose exposure leads to the worst outcomes.

Top vulnerabilities

Risk = likelihood × impact (1–25). Click a row to see the evidence, how the score was built, the standards behind the rule, and the fix.

IDSeverityRisk L×IFindingAffected APISourcesPaths
F-001critical25 5×5Administrative function reachable by ordinary callers
API5 · API5:2023		POST /api/v1/orderOtherService/orderOther/admin
ts-order-other-service		4

What was found

POST /api/v1/orderOtherService/orderOther/admin (ts-order-other-service): publicly routed as /api/v1/orderOtherService/orderOther/admin; 1 anonymous 2xx

An admin / internal / export function is reachable from outside its intended audience (publicly routed or answered anonymously).

Evidence (high confidence)

  • publicly routed as /api/v1/orderOtherService/orderOther/admin
  • 1 anonymous 2xx

Sources: callchain, infrastructure, openapi, runtime_traffic

Why score 25 (critical)

  • likelihood base 4
  • impact base 5
  • likelihood +1: reachable from the internet

Leads to: Sensitive data exposure. Best attack path APCR 25.

Recommendation

Restrict /api/v1/orderOtherService/orderOther/admin to an admin role and remove it from public routing.

  1. Require an admin role on the function, checked in the service.
  2. Do not route admin paths through the public gateway; expose them on a separate internal listener.

Based on

F-005critical20 5×4Sensitive operation answers anonymous callers
TS-01 · API2:2023		DELETE /api/v1/orderservice/order/{orderId}
ts-order-service		3

What was found

DELETE /api/v1/orderservice/order/{orderId} (ts-order-service) returned 2xx to 1 request(s) without a token

Requests with no credential at all got a 2xx response from an endpoint that returns sensitive data or changes state.

Evidence (high confidence)

  • 1 anonymous 2xx responses
  • data returned: none; method DELETE

Sources: callchain, openapi, runtime_traffic

Why score 20 (critical)

  • likelihood base 4
  • impact base 4
  • likelihood +1: anonymous success seen on the public path
  • likelihood +1: reachable from the internet

Leads to: Sensitive data exposure. Best attack path APCR 20.

Recommendation

Add authentication to DELETE /api/v1/orderservice/order/{orderId} in ts-order-service.

  1. Require a verified token on this operation in the service itself, not only at the gateway.
  2. Reject requests without Authorization with 401 before any business logic runs.
  3. Add a test that calls the endpoint anonymously and expects 401.
# FastAPI
@app.get('/admin/transactions')
def admin_tx(user = Depends(require_role('admin'))):
    ...

  • impact base 4

What was found

route /api/v1/routeplanservice/** -> ts-route-plan-service has auth: none

A gateway route is configured with no authentication and forwards to endpoints that are not login endpoints, so the gateway is not acting as an authentication boundary.

Evidence (high confidence)

  • defined in /home/claude/api-threat-graph/bench/testbeds/trainticket/gateway/application.yml (route route-plan)
  • exposes: POST /api/v1/routeplanservice/routePlan/cheapestRoute, POST /api/v1/routeplanservice/routePlan/minStopStations, POST /api/v1/routeplanservice/routePlan/quickestRoute, GET /api/v1/routeplanservice/welcome

Sources: infrastructure, runtime_traffic

Why score 16 (high)

  • likelihood base 4
  • impact base 4

Leads to: Sensitive data exposure. Best attack path APCR 16.

Recommendation

Set auth: required on gateway route /api/v1/routeplanservice.

  1. Set auth: required on the route, or split public paths (login) into their own route.
  2. Deny by default: routes without an explicit auth setting should be rejected at deploy time.
routes:
  - prefix: /api/payments
    service: payment-service
    auth: required      # was: none

whole service		1

What was found

ts-delivery-service does not set runAsNonRoot

Nothing stops the container process from running as UID 0 (runAsUser: 0, or no runAsNonRoot).

Evidence (medium confidence)

  • runAsNonRoot missing

Sources: infrastructure

Why score 3 (low)

  • likelihood base 2
  • impact base 3
  • likelihood -1: service reachable only inside the cluster

Leads to: Container / cluster compromise. Best attack path APCR 1.5.

Recommendation

Run ts-delivery-service as a non-root user.

  1. Set runAsNonRoot: true and a non-zero runAsUser.
  2. Build images with a non-root USER.
